articles.title: Matt Fitzpatrick casts doubt on Dubai title defence over fears of ongoing conflict
articles.summary: World No 4 may snub World Tour Championship. ‘I’m not comfortable playing in the Middle East’ Matt Fitzpatrick, the world No 4, has admitted to reservations over appearing at the DP World Tour’s end of season events in Abu Dhabi and Dubai because of the conflict in the Middle East.
body: Fitzpatrick even suggested Formula One is reconsidering staging the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix in December after races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were called off this year due to the Iran war, though it remains on the calendar.

The Abu Dhabi Championship is due to take place from 5 November, with the DP World Tour Championship slated for the following week. Every indication is that those competitions will happen in the United Arab Emirates, despite contingencies involving Turkey, Spain and Portugal known to have been considered.

“As things stand right now, I would say I’m not that comfortable [playing in the Middle East],” Fitzpatrick said. “A few things have changed for me. I had a child in August and that changes things a bit more.

“It would feel a little bit weird, given what I’m reading elsewhere. Things can change overnight, I’m sure. I think it seems to be going down that path of things are getting better. I’ve looked on the UK [government] website, I know they changed it from essential travel only to one step better than that.

articles.title: 'Let's go, let's go' - inside catastrophic derby VAR mistake
articles.summary: The controversy surrounding the VAR decision to allow Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby has rumbled on for days, so what led to the error?
body: The words of video assistant referee Matt Donohue as he rushed through the review to award Erling Haaland's winning goal in the Manchester derby.
No doubt Donohue was simply trying to be as efficient as possible, but it led to one of the most catastrophic VAR errors the Premier League has seen.
Donohue and his assistant VAR, Blake Antrobus, inexplicably failed to notice that Enzo Fernandez was three yards offside before he tried to head the ball.
Refereeing has always been a goldfish bowl of scrutiny and pressure, heightened by the introduction of VAR.

articles.title: Fitzpatrick not '100% comfortable' with tour finals in Dubai
articles.summary: Matt Fitzpatrick says he is not "100% comfortable" with the prospect of travelling to Dubai for the season-ending DP World Tour Championship in November when he is due to be defending champion.
body: Fitzpatrick is concerned that the United Arab Emirates could be a target in the ongoing conflict between Iran, the United States and Israel.
"You've only got to look at the hotel that got hit earlier this year," Fitzpatrick told BBC Sport. "I was having dinner the week I won in that hotel.
"That's obviously very scary when you think about how it was a few months away but how close you were to that particular spot and for something like that to happen. It's obviously quite scary."

Fitzpatrick would like to see the event switched to a different host country, a decision he called a "no brainer, in my opinion" before adding: "But I'm not a sponsor, I'm not paying the bills and all that sort of stuff.

articles.title: What's gone wrong for Chelsea talent Kendry Paez?
articles.summary: Kendry Paez was one of the world's best young talents when Chelsea signed him as a 16-year-old. Three years later, he's playing for the Under-21s. So what has gone wrong?
body: Attacking midfielder Kendry Paez has finally pulled on a Chelsea shirt, three years after agreeing a move to Stamford Bridge - albeit for the club's Under-21s.
Chelsea agreed a £17.27m deal to sign Paez from Ecuadorian side Independiente del Valle in 2023 when he was 16, but his development has not progressed as quickly as many expected.
Now 19, Paez made his first appearance in Chelsea colours for Cobham Next Gen, the club's newly-renamed Under-21 side, as a 12th-minute substitute in a 4-1 win away to Arsenal on Saturday.
It comes after new manager Xabi Alonso said the midfielder was "not in my plans" and Chelsea listed him as an academy player on the club website.

articles.title: 4 takeaways from Broncos' snap counts in Week 1
articles.summary: There was quite a bit to take away from the Denver Broncos ' embarrassing loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday night, and nearly all of it was negative. The Broncos were outplayed and outworked in every phase of the game and Andy Reid and his coaching staff outperformed Sean Payton and his…
body: Looking at the team's snap counts from this game, here are some interesting things we took away from them.
The Broncos never established much of a rushing attack in this game, so it was tough to get into a groove running the ball. J.K. Dobbins led the way with eight carries and RJ Harvey only had three.

But Jonah Coleman, whom the Broncos used a fourth-round pick on, saw only three offensive snaps and he didn't touch the ball one time. This is something the team should focus on changing, particularly if it faces any short-yardage situations in Week 2.
This game got away from them, but you brought Coleman in to help grind out those tough yards, so leaving him dressed on the sideline with hardly any work should not become a habit.

articles.title: Winter Olympic venues confirmed with events in two countries
articles.summary: The sporting venues for the 2030 Winter Games are confirmed, with events to be held in Lyon and the French Alps - except speed skating, which will take place in the Netherlands.
body: Events will take place at 11 competition venues, external primarily across southern France with the location allocation for ice sports and alpine skiing confirmed by the International Olympic Committee (IOC)on Wednesday.
Lyon will host curling, figure skating and short track speed skating across three sites, including Parc Olympique Lyonnais, the home of the Ligue 1 side.
Courchevel will host the Alpine skiing speed events – the downhill and super-G, including team events – while Val d'Isere stages the slalom events.
The announcement finalises the venues after a turbulent few months for 2030 Games organisers, which included several changes to original plans.

articles.title: F1 announce 2027 calendar and increase in Sprint rounds
articles.summary: Formula 1 has announced its 2027 calendar and an increase in the number of Sprint weekends from six to 10, with the season starting in Bahrain.
body: For a fourth consecutive year, there are 24 rounds scheduled with Portugal's Portimao and Turkey's Istanbul Park returning to the calendar.

As expected, the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort falls off the schedule while the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya moves into a rotational deal with Spa-Francorchamps that will see the Spanish event held in even numbered years from 2028 and the Belgian Grand Prix held in odd numbered years from 2027.

F1 had delayed its calendar announcement for next year due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which has created uncertainty over the end of the current season with Qatar and Abu Dhabi still currently scheduled to take place later this year.
Bahrain will host a four-day pre-season test on February 24-27 before holding the 2027 season-opener on March 12-14 and it will be a Sprint weekend, with the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix a week later.

articles.title: Arsenal? Chelsea? Man City? Which club has most valuable teens?
articles.summary: The Premier League's teenage sensations are making headlines after Max Dowman's starring display for Arsenal and JJ Gabriel's revelation that he wants to leave Manchester United.
body: Dowman, 16, scored twice in Arsenal's Carabao Cup win over Ipswich, only hours after 15-year-old Gabriel had stunned Manchester United with his request to cancel his registration at the club.
Dowman's breakthrough and Gabriel's desire for first-team opportunities show how the stars of tomorrow are starting younger, but which Premier League clubs have the most valuable teens?

For this week's Between the Lines, we use Transfermarkt valuations to rank Premier League clubs by teenage value, albeit with the caveat that Transfermarkt does not assign valuations to young players with no first-team experience such as Gabriel.
According to Transfermarkt, Manchester City have the most valuable teenagers at a combined £122.6m, putting them just ahead of Chelsea on £121m, and Arsenal in third on £102.4m.

articles.title: DP World Tour unveils big changes to 2027 schedule
articles.summary: The DP World Tour has announced a new date for the 2027 BMW PGA Championship, as it unveiled a series of big schedule changes for next year's calendar.
body: The tour also confirmed the return of three national opens, a significant step in its plans to grow, with DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings confirming the series will now host 17 national opens across the 2027 season.
After a seven-year absence, the Hong Kong Open will return to the DP World Tour calendar, and the Deutsche Bank Singapore Open has also been added back to the schedule.
Meanwhile, the tour has also confirmed the Open de Portugal | Cascais-Lisboa will return to the calendar.
The DP World Tour has also made a series of adjustments to its Closing Swing and Back 9, with the 2027 Ryder Cup to take place at Adare Manor between September 17 and 19.
